name: gateway stills — a synchronous engine, no GPU anywhere in the path
_why: OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-09-01: stills route back to the Lovable gateway and the GPU leaves the still path, because the RunPod worker had never drawn a frame on the current endpoint and every film was dying at `still 1`. The gateway answers in ONE call — `start` carries the frame — so this scenario proves the worker takes it without polling. The failure it exists to catch is expensive: a worker that polled a synchronous engine would earn a 400 per shot, and a future `poll` that redrew instead of refusing would bill a second image per shot forever. `key: null` is the other half — a gateway still is bytes that were never stored, so in-house motion cannot animate one. This is a CLASSIC grade, which is what the directive's era actually shipped: gateway stills under ONIQ's own Ken Burns, with Veo reserved for movie grade.

job.prompt: a brave mouse in a bakery

plan.title: The Mouse Under the Bakery
plan.setting: a warm old bakery at night, flour dust in the lamplight

shots.still: A small brown mouse peers out from under a wooden floorboard.
shots.narration: Under the floorboards of an old bakery there lived a very small and very brave mouse.

shots.still: Wide view of the dark bakery, moonlight on the counters.
shots.narration: Every night when the baker went home, the mouse came out to see what the world had left behind.

shots.still: The mouse carries a crumb twice its size across the floor.
shots.narration: And every night she carried home one crumb, which to a mouse is a very great treasure indeed.
